local_review.finding_body: The current-defaults lanes on JDK 25 and latest EA and the future-defaults-all lane all showed libfreenect2 selecting `OpenGLDepthPacketProcessor`, reporting that `DISPLAY` was missing, and terminating the JVM/native test process with exit 255. The failing `openDefaultDevice()` assertion exercised a known-broken environmental path in a test premised on having no Kinect attached, contrary to §FS-test-contract.2.6; stable enumeration and serial-number behavior should be tested instead.
local_review.finding_title: Avoid libfreenect2 default-device probes in headless tests
local_review.fix_note: Removed the `openDefaultDevice()` no-hardware probe and its unused import from `Libfreenect2Test`. Verified headlessly with `javaTest`, full current-defaults tests on latest EA and GraalVM 25, and full `future-defaults-all` tests on latest EA. Also passed coordinate Checkstyle, Spotless, metadata validation, index validation, library-stats generation/validation, `git diff --check`, and `fissile check --staged`.
local_review.review_comment: All three required metadata-test lanes failed reproducibly because the no-device test called `openDefaultDevice()`, which selected libfreenect2's default OpenGL pipeline and terminated the headless test process when `DISPLAY` was unavailable. I removed that broken environmental probe while retaining the test's public no-device enumeration and serial-number assertions. I reviewed the complete single-coordinate diff under the new-library rules: the tests remain non-scaffold public-API tests in a separate package with no version-pinned test logic, Native Image dodge, build/run flag, legacy metadata file, or coverage-gate violation; the reported 0/0 dynamic-access result remains a valid no-calls case. The repaired tree passes all affected lanes and is approved.
